# Website publication and benchmark downloads

The canonical benchmark data remain under `Benchmarks/results/`. `tools/generateBenchmarkWebsiteDocumentation.m` generates the benchmark page, figures, and `docs/benchmarks/downloads.json` from the benchmark catalog. Each download entry records its public URL, repository source, SHA-256, and byte length. Multiple public URLs may point to the same source file.

`docs:build` and `docs:check` require Python 3 on PATH in addition to the existing MATLAB documentation dependencies. They keep download payloads out of the committed documentation tree. Validation copies the generated tree into temporary storage, materializes downloads with `tools/website_downloads.py`, and checks the resulting links. The Python tool independently checks the exact catalog-derived download mapping and hashes; it rejects missing, extra, unsafe, or conflicting entries. `docs:check` compares the committed and generated trees before materialization.

The `Publish website` workflow builds the committed documentation with Jekyll and stages the downloads without running MATLAB. Pull requests build and verify the site but cannot deploy. Relevant pushes to `main`, and manual dispatches from `main`, deploy the verified artifact through the `github-pages` environment. GitHub Pages must use **GitHub Actions** as its publishing source. The custom domain remains `wavevortexmodel.org`; every existing `/benchmarks/data/` and `/benchmarks/raw/` URL retains its original JSON bytes.

Both rendered CI and publication call the same staging tool before Jekyll and verify download hashes again after rendering. Download files must never be added to `docs/benchmarks/data/` or `docs/benchmarks/raw/` in Git. Repository checks reject these paths even if someone adds an artifact registration. Only the compact manifest is registered; new canonical scientific data still require their own exact registration and publication review.

## Migration verification

The immutable pre-migration revision is `a2e368e677b00dedec6cb11d8cbbf1404fbed5b6`. Its 24 generated JSON files (17 normalized datasets and seven raw downloads) total 15,806,546 bytes. Each old `docs` path corresponds to the manifest entry whose URL is that path without the `docs` prefix. Migration verification compares every old Git blob with its canonical source and staged/rendered download. The canonical data, catalog, scoring references, and historical artifact baseline remain unchanged. The 24 old copies were registered published assets, so only their exact registrations are removed; historical-output retirement rules are unchanged. Ordinary Git history preserves the old copies.

Before changing the Pages setting, require a successful pull-request website build, download/hash checks, and the existing required CI aggregate. Switch the publishing source to GitHub Actions before merging the deletion so the legacy branch publisher cannot publish a tree without its staged downloads. After merge, verify the first deployment, the custom domain, and all 24 live download URLs. A rollback can restore the previous source tree from the recorded revision and republish through the Actions workflow.
